title: Cross-Region AdmitSignal Index and Synthetic Golden-Probe Dashboard
creator: Marta Liu
description:
Objective: Define and implement an AdmitSignal index (per-tenant, per-shard, per-region) that summarizes admission pressure and spill behavior into a single -0..100 score, wire that index into synthetic golden-probes that run from each region, and build a Grafana dashboard that exposes correlation between AdmitSignal, token-level latency SLIs, KV-prefetch hits, and failover decisions.

Background: We currently have many token-level SLI dashboards but lack a compact, queryable index that surfaces admission pressure patterns that precede multi-region failovers and circuit-shedding events. During recent incidents we observed that admit-rate oscillations + KV-miss bursts were the leading indicators before p99 tail spikes and subsequent region fallback. This ticket consolidates instrumentation and a first-pass UI to make those signals actionable by on-call and SRE.

Success criteria (MUST):
- Implement AdmitSignal calculation at aggregator: inputs = admit_score_histogram (0..100), regional_kv_miss_rate, queue_depth_percentile, early_exit_rate. Score must be stored as timeseries (Prometheus metric: redwood_admit_signal{tenant,region,shard}).
- Add eBPF-based microprobe to capture precise token timing (ingress->dispatch->decode start) for synthetic probes and surface kv_prefetch_hit label. Probe implementation must be opt-in and low overhead.
- Create three dashboard views in Grafana: 1) AdmitSignal heatmap (tenant x region over time); 2) Tokenized waterfall explorer (sampled traces for synthetic probes showing admit delay, dispatch latency, kv wait, decode); 3) Failover readiness panel showing correlation between AdmitSignal spikes and automatic circuit transitions.
- Run synthetic golden-probe job in every region every 30s for two weeks; capture baseline and alert on delta > 15 for 1h.
- Document runbook steps for on-call (playbook link below) and link to rollout plan.

Telemetry definition / metric names:
- redwood_admit_signal{tenant,region,shard} gauge
- redwood_admit_components{tenant,region,shard,label="admit_score|kv_miss|queue_p95|early_exit"} gauge
- redwood_token_probe_duration_ms{probe_type,region,tenant,synthetic=true} histogram
- redwood_kv_prefetch_hit_ratio{region,shard} gauge

Design notes:
- AdmitSignal is a weighted sum normalized to 0..100; weight tuning lives in runtime-config and default weights mirror production-smoke heuristics. The aggregator implements a sliding 1m window with decay to avoid noise-flapping.
- Synthetic probes will exercise a fixed 128-token request with deterministic prefix to maximize KV-prefetch path coverage. We will tag probes so they are ignored for customer billing.
- eBPF probe only captures timestamps and syscall context; sampling set to 1/100 during rollout and 1/10 on canary tenants.

Dashboard panels (first iteration):
- AdmitSignal Heatmap: rows = tenants (top N by QPS), cols = regions, color = median AdmitSignal over 5m, click -> time range filter.
- Token Waterfall Explorer: waterfall per synthetic probe sample showing stages and annotations for admit/queue/kv/decode; supports selecting any sample to open trace link.
- KV-prefetch Scatter: x=kv_prefetch_hit_ratio, y=p99 token duration, point size = QPS; color = region.
- Failover Trigger Timeline: timeline of circuit state transitions with AdmitSignal overlay and synthetic probe anomalies.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement metric emission in aggregator (feature branch runtime/admit-index) behind feature flag.
2) Deploy eBPF probe as opt-in package to canary region (us-west-2) on small subset of hosts.
3) Enable synthetic job and dashboard in staging; run for 3 days and validate.
4) Ramp to all regions, gradually increasing eBPF sampling to target.
5) Flip feature flag to enable on production aggregator.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for index calculation with randomized inputs.
- Integration test harness that replays admission traces and asserts index correlates with expected label.
- Load test in canary region to prove <1% CPU overhead for aggregator and <2% latency inflation for worker processes when eBPF enabled at sampling 1/10.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: eBPF sampling overhead causes worker jank. Mitigation: default opt-in; limit to canary and 1/100 sampling.
- Risk: noisy index thresholds cause pager fatigue. Mitigation: create separate alerting rules for 'admit spike' vs 'sustained high', require multi-metric corroboration.

Follow-ups / future work:
- Expose admit index in Console and per-route breakdowns.
- Automatic runbook suggestions (linking a surge to specific tenant configs).
